text.p: Finnish cargo shipping group Finnlines Oy on Wednesday sought to clarify an earlier full-year 1997 profit outlook, group treasurer Seija Turunen said.
"We have actually clarified our forecast for full-year profit," Turunen told Reuters.

A previous forecast -- that full-year 1997 operating earnings would remain at par with 1996 -- had by assumption excluded a 115 million markka profit on the sale of forwarding unit Huolintakeskus, although this had been booked as operating profit for accounting reasons, she said.
That outlook was published in Finnlines' 1996 annual report in February, and Turunen said a statement on Wednesday with Finnlines' January-April results sought to clarify this.
That statement said: "Finnlines' full-year result is, however, expected to remain below the previous year's level, which included a profit of FIM 115 million on the Huolintakeskus sale."
In 1996, Finnlines posted a 404 million markka profit before extraordinary items and a 444 million markka operating profit.
